dedupe_keys.name: hornsdale power reserve south australia s 150 mw grid scale battery

description: The Hornsdale Power Reserve, owned and operated by Neoen Australia and known as the South Australian Big Battery, was billed as the world's first big battery and provides grid-support services in the National Electricity Market. The first 100 MW / 129 MWh stage was completed in November 2017 next to the Hornsdale Wind Farm about 15 km north of Jamestown; in its first two years it confirmed the benefits of grid-scale batteries and saved South Australian consumers more than 150 million dollars. A 50 MW / 64.5 MWh expansion was finished in September 2020, and the full 150 MW was upgraded with Tesla's Virtual Machine Mode so it can supply inertia support. The site covers project overview, benefits for the local economy, consumers and community, the project lifecycle and visitor information. Coverage is one site in South Australia's transmission network. Access: the public project website, free to read; no licence is stated and the page carries a company copyright notice. Caveats: an owner-published account with headline claims and no data files, and independent evaluation reports must be found separately. It suits operations and control studies of frequency response and inertia from batteries and grid resilience appraisal, and no other related records are catalogued yet.
